textbookBox.concept: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its force can be felt. Field lines go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its force can be felt. Field lines go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.
beats.speakEn: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its force can be felt. Field lines go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.

beats.en: Field lines never cross each other, and closer lines mean a stronger field.
beats.speakEn: Field lines never cross each other, and closer lines mean a stronger field.

Rule: Field lines never cross each other, and closer lines mean a stronger field.

textbookBox.concept: A current-carrying straight wire produces circular field lines around it. The direction is given by the right-hand thumb rule.

beats.en: Hold the wire in your right hand with the thumb along the current; the curled fingers show the field direction.
